document.title: Commvault REST API Reference (Job Operations, Authentication Operations)

capability_sources.note: Endpoint path, query parameters (jobFilter, jobCategory, completedJobLookupTime), and the complete response field set were confirmed directly from the official api.commvault.com machine-generated reference page, which shows a literal, complete example JSON response: {"totalRecordsWithoutPaging": N, "jobs": [{"jobSummary": {"jobId", "status", "jobType", "percentComplete", "jobStartTime", "subclientName", "destClientName", "subclient": {"clientName", ...}, ...}}]}. Only the status vocabulary directly evidenced across this page and Commvault's own REST API / cvpysdk documentation (Completed, Running, Waiting, Suspended, Killed) is modeled; Commvault's own documentation states the complete status vocabulary is longer, so an unrecognized value maps to an honest UNKNOWN rather than being guessed.

authentication_source.note: Confirmed directly from Commvault's own official documentation page, which shows the exact endpoint (`POST $[webservice]/Login`), request body fields (username, password [Base64 UTF-8 encoded], domain, commserver, timeout), and the response token field (`"token": "QSDK ..."`). A second independent official source (api.commvault.com's AuthenticationOperations/login page) corroborated the `Authtoken` header requirement for subsequent requests -- a genuine, confirmed difference from every other connector built for this project, which all use either a vendor-specific token header (X-Auth-Token, vmware-api-session-id) or Authorization: Bearer/Basic, never a header literally named Authtoken. Token validity: 30 minutes of inactivity by default. Logout (`POST webservice/Logout` with the same Authtoken header, no body) was confirmed the same way. This connector follows the established login -> read -> logout bounded-cycle pattern used for both Huawei connectors and vCenter, never caching a live session.

self_test_source.note: No confirmed dedicated version/compatibility endpoint independent of the job-status read was found; the self-test reuses a narrow, one-hour-lookback job-status read itself, the same pattern used for every prior connector's probe.

unconfirmed_gaps: The complete Commvault job-status vocabulary is longer than what could be independently confirmed via real, working examples during connector construction; only Completed/Running/Waiting/Suspended/Killed are modeled, and any other value (e.g. a partial-success or specific failure-reason status) maps to UNKNOWN rather than being guessed at a severity.

Client inventory (GET webservice/Client) is a real, confirmed endpoint that was not implemented in this first pass -- only the job-status health signal was built. There is also no confirmed field connecting a Commvault-protected client to entities from any other connector in this project, so no graph relationship (e.g. BACKED_BY) is asserted.

Backup policy, storage policy, and recovery-point/point-in-time catalog concepts are real Commvault domain concepts with their own REST API surface that were not implemented here; this connector is scoped to job-status health only.
